summary: Read-only frontend check of the laptop layout fix (breakpoint moved to 960px / coarse-pointer / no-hover). For each page I recorded the layout of every element (position and size, display, grid columns, font size, margin, padding) twice: once as it is now, and once on the same page with the '@layer responsive' stylesheet switched off in the browser only. That second version stands in for the old, pre-responsive layout. Covered 9 routes (all 8 public pages plus one field-note detail) at 961, 1024, 1080, 1280 and 1366 on preview data, and at 1024 and 1280 on read-only production fixtures. Result: on preview, 0 elements differ outside the coloured bands at any of these widths. The only difference is the band element itself on Craft and Workshops, which is the allowed edge alignment. Header menu is horizontal with the MENU button hidden. Home Field Notes keeps two columns (title and intro on the left, featured object on the right, original margin). The /field-notes hero keeps two columns. Craft and Theatre hero text still sits on top of the image. Connect has two columns. At 960px the responsive layout switches on as intended (MENU button, single columns). On production fixtures, the remaining differences come from images still loading, not from the stylesheet: the same page measured twice with no CSS change differed by 22-29 elements. On Theatre the band boxing changes height, which pushes the footer down; this is allowed. Touch devices at 390, 768, 1024 and 1366 still get the MENU button and responsive layouts. On each, opening Our Work then tapping Field Notes or Connect works, the links are not covered, they navigate correctly, and there is no horizontal overflow. No editor controls appear, even with ?edit=1. Desktop hover menu at 961, 1024 and 1080: Our Work opens on hover, the first link is clickable and navigates, and the menu closes when the mouse leaves. All API calls were replayed from saved fixtures. Every non-GET request was blocked. No data was written, nothing was published, no app source was changed.

design_issues.screen: Home Field Notes cards at 1024-1080 (fine pointer) - EXISTED BEFORE, not caused by this fix
issues: The card description texts overlap the next card's text ('In a courtyard...' runs into 'Flowers, birds...', which runs into 'A brightly coloured...'). Overlap area is about 1000-2100px². The same overlap appears with the responsive layer switched off, so this comes from the saved desktop sizes. No overlap at 1280 and wider.

design_issues.screen: Production fixtures at 1024: Home band a3457c65 and Workshops band - EXISTED BEFORE
issues: Text runs past the right edge of the coloured band: 40px on Home ('A restored building can find n...') and 19px on Workshops ('For generations, people have l...'). The reference layout without the responsive layer has the same band box and the same overflow, so this is not new. Fine at 1280.

action_items: No regression found; the fix restores the original laptop layout from 961px on fine-pointer screens.

Optional, only if the user wants it (not a regression): the Home Field Notes card text overlap at 1024-1080 and the band text overflow on production at 1024 both come from saved desktop sizes and existed before the responsive work.
critical_code_review_comments: responsive.css has three separate blocks using the same '@media (max-width: 960px), (hover: none), (pointer: coarse)' condition. They could be merged, or the condition kept in one place, so future breakpoint changes cannot drift apart. Small cleanup, no effect on behaviour.

The editor is hidden from 1024px down while the desktop layout starts at 961px. So between 961 and 1024px a fine-pointer user sees the desktop layout without editor controls. This matches the intended editor gate (1025px+ with fine pointer and hover).
seed_data_creation: None. Saved fixtures in /app/test_reports/responsive_fixtures were replayed. Non-GET requests were blocked.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The comparison is done by setting sheet.disabled on the stylesheet that contains '@layer responsive' (TOGGLE_JS in iter31_laptop_fidelity.py). On production fixtures, scroll the page first (settle() in iter31_band_spill.py) so lazy-loaded images finish; otherwise loading shifts show up as false differences. Menu test ids: nav-m-about, nav-m-work, nav-m-work-toggle, nav-m-notes, nav-m-connect, mobile-menu-toggle. Headless Chromium reports hover and a fine pointer; contexts with has_touch=True report a coarse pointer and no hover.
